source.title_on_document: Iterative Research Idea Development Through Evolving and Composing Idea Facets with Literature-Grounded Feedback

supplement.where: Appendices A-I in the supplied PDF, pp. 21-31; Appendix G spans pp. 23-25. A separate external supplement is not stated.
supplement.holds: Participant demographics, task instructions, qualitative analysis themes, full survey questions (Table 5), full survey-result plots and significance markers (Figure 8), and LLM prompts.

paper_design_summary: An eight-person formative study combined artifact walkthroughs, a Google Docs/Perplexity AI Wizard-of-Oz ideation activity, and thematic interview analysis (p. 4, Section 3). In a counterbalanced within-subjects comparison, 20 computer-science PhD students and postdocs developed research briefs for 30 minutes per condition using IdeaSynth and a baseline with the same LLM; outcomes were participants' self-ratings and interaction logs, with no independent or computed creativity score for their briefs (pp. 12-15, Sections 5.1-5.3). Seven lab participants subsequently used IdeaSynth on their own projects for at least three days and at least one hour total, followed by interviews analyzed thematically (p. 16, Section 6).

arms.name: Baseline

participants.exclusions: No exclusions stated. 20 recruited; each person did both conditions, so 20 people in total, not 40.
participants.who: Computer-science researchers pursuing or holding a PhD (graduate students and postdocs): 12 HCI, 8 NLP; 11 men, 8 women, 1 nonbinary
participants.country: U.S. and Canada (Table 3, country where the participant conducts research)
participants.quote: We recruited 20 researchers (11M, 8F, 1 nonbinary) who are pursuing or have completed their Ph.D. degrees (i.e., graduate students and postdocs) in Computer Science
participants.locator: p. 12, Section 5.1.1 Participants; p. 22, Appendix D, Table 3

ai_tool.name_model: IdeaSynth built on gpt-4-turbo (temperature 0.7); gpt-3.5-turbo for paper processing; baseline uses the same LLM setup
ai_tool.how_used: Treatment: AI suggests clarifying questions, alternative and expanded idea-facet nodes, edge feedback, and composes a research brief from selected nodes. Baseline: chat-style Q&A and an AI rewrite of the editor text. AI available in both arms (pp. 11-12, Sections 4.3-4.4; p. 12, Section 5.1.2).

task.description: Develop a research idea on an assigned broad topic into a research brief of about 12 sentences (problem and RQ, design and solution, evaluation method, contribution and impact). HCI topics: AI-augmented tools for creativity, human-AI collaboration in data analysis. NLP topics: LLM-as-a-judge, biases in LLMs.
task.duration: 30 minutes per task, two tasks; session about 90 minutes (p. 12, Section 5.1.4)

outcomes.name: Self-assessed novelty of own research brief (7-point agreement scale)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Both conditions provided LLM assistance during ideation, and the survey followed each task (p. 12, Sections 5.1.2 and 5.1.4). Participant self-assessment of their own brief on a 7-point agreement scale, not an independent output score (pp. 12-13, Section 5.2; p. 23, Appendix G, Table 5). Primary/secondary status is not stated.

contrasts.reported: No numeric means printed for novelty; text: 'measuring participants' ratings on the five dimensions—Novelty, Impact, Specificity, Feasibility, and Relevance ... independently, we did not identify a significant difference between conditions for any metrics.' Fig. 8 (violin plots, Wilcoxon signed-rank) does not mark Novelty as significant.

outcomes.name: Self-reported 'I was able to sufficiently explore and evaluate alternative versions of my research ideas' (Exploring Research Ideas, 7-point scale)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Both conditions provided LLM assistance during ideation, and the survey followed each task (p. 12, Sections 5.1.2 and 5.1.4). Self-reported exploration on a 7-point agreement scale (p. 23, Appendix G, Table 5). Coded paper_primary because exploration is explicitly one of four pre-selected key survey measures (p. 13, Section 5.2; p. 14, Figure 7). The reported MANOVA F tests Impact, Feasibility, Literature Grounding, and Sufficient Exploration jointly.

contrasts.reported: IdeaSynth mean = 5.40, SD = 1.50 vs baseline mean = 3.65, SD = 1.60, p < 0.01. One of four pre-selected measures in a MANOVA on Impact, Feasibility, Literature Grounding, and Sufficient Exploration: manova F = 3.30, p < 0.05.

outcomes.name: Self-reported 'I was able to effectively expand on my initial research idea with more details' (Expanding Research Idea, 7-point scale)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Both conditions provided LLM assistance during ideation, and the survey followed each task (p. 12, Sections 5.1.2 and 5.1.4). Self-reported expansion on a 7-point agreement scale (p. 23, Appendix G, Table 5); the Figure 8 significance marker treats this item independently (p. 25). Primary/secondary status is not stated.

contrasts.reported: IdeaSynth mean = 6.05, SD = 0.89 vs baseline mean = 4.45, SD = 2.04; Fig. 8 marks 'Expanding Research Idea**' (p < 0.01, Wilcoxon signed-rank, question treated independently).

arms.name: Google Docs/Perplexity AI Wizard-of-Oz probe
arms.description: Single ideation activity using shared Google Docs, pre-generated research ideas, and participant requests relayed to Perplexity AI by a facilitator.

participants.exclusions: No exclusions stated; recruitment continued until data saturation.
participants.who: HCI and NLP researchers: PhD students and postdoctoral researchers; 5 men and 3 women.
participants.country: U.S., Canada, and South Korea (Table 1: country where the participant primarily conducts research)
participants.quote: We conducted a formative study with 8 HCI and NLP researchers (5M, 3F) both to understand the challenges in existing ideation workflows and also to identify design opportunities for enhancing research ideation with AI.
participants.locator: p. 4, Section 3 Formative Study; p. 21, Appendix A, Table 1

ai_tool.name_model: Perplexity AI with Academic Focus; underlying model not stated
ai_tool.how_used: Initial research ideas were generated from participants' research interests and publications. During the activity, a facilitator forwarded participant requests from Google Docs to Perplexity AI and pasted the responses into a second shared document. Participants could develop, combine, or disregard the supplied ideas (p. 4, Section 3; p. 21, Appendix B).

task.description: Walk through an existing research-project artifact, develop a research idea using the design probe, write a short paragraph describing the idea, and reflect in an exit interview. Transcripts underwent open coding and thematic analysis; no creativity or diversity score was assigned to the produced idea (p. 4, Section 3; p. 21, Appendix C, Table 2).
task.duration: Around 60 minutes overall, including around 25 minutes working with the ideation probe (p. 4, Section 3).

eligibility.reason: The comparative lab study analyzed 20 people, each using both systems, below the 50-person threshold (p. 12, Sections 5.1.1-5.1.2). It is a counterbalanced within-subjects comparison with randomization not stated, so the design is other and criterion 1 remains unclear (p. 12, Section 5.1.4). Both arms use generative AI, making the contrast ai_design. The reported creativity-related outcomes are participants' self-ratings; interaction logs measure system use, and no independent rater or computed creativity/diversity measure scores the briefs (pp. 12-15, Sections 5.2-5.3.5; p. 18, Section 7.4.2). The formative study has 8 participants and qualitative thematic analysis, with no randomized comparison or qualifying output score (p. 4, Section 3; p. 21, Appendices A-C). The deployment study has 7 participants drawn from the lab sample, no comparison group, and thematic interview outcomes (p. 16, Section 6). No study meets all core criteria or a context category.

one_line_finding: With 20 CS researchers in a counterbalanced within-subjects lab study, IdeaSynth raised self-rated exploration of alternatives (5.40 vs 3.65, p < 0.01) and self-rated idea expansion (6.05 vs 4.45) over an LLM baseline, but self-rated novelty, impact, specificity, feasibility, and relevance did not differ significantly (pp. 13, 15, Figs. 7-8).
